content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in the short term (first 5–10 days) after sentiment spikes (sentiment > 0.5), especially when sentiment is high and recent.
- Overshoots occur after sharp upward sentiment moves; model reacts too aggressively, peaking too early and then correcting sharply.
- When sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.2), model tends to underestimate, often missing the downward trend until late in the horizon.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert to recent mean, especially after 10–15 days.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — model fails to capture the “pullback” phase after initial spike.
- Sentiment decay matters: if sentiment drops below 0.3 within 3–5 days, model should reduce forecast slope and avoid sharp downward revisions.
- Model ignores sentiment momentum: if sentiment is rising, model should not overreact to recent price spikes; if falling, should not ignore early price corrections.
